newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Socialists call for more talks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Socialists call for more talks.

text.p: Bulgaria's embattled Socialist rulers invited their opponents for talks on Monday but warned that if the talks failed they would present a new Socialist cabinet to parliament on Tuesday.

A party statement offered negotiations with the mediation of President Petar Stoyanov on formation of a new cabinet. The opposition, which wants immediate elections, has held one round of talks with the Socialists then refused to meet them again.
"If there is no agreement with the political forces, parliament will vote on the cabinet proposed by the Democratic Left," said the statement.

It said the Socialists were prepared to discuss a cabinet with the mandate of other parliamentary groups, but Socialist leader Georgi Parvanov said he expected his majority party to be represented in any cabinet.

The cabinet should prepare a new state budget, legal measures for introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime and other steps to tackle the economic crisis, and should hold negotiations with the International Monetary Fund, the statement said.
Parvanov said that once the crisis was stabilised, the cabinet could transform itself into an interim, caretaker administration at the end of April and organise elections in June.
